commander.satan: The quartermaster asked Pavel "Tin" Satan to sign for the blanket. He examined the blanket and asked whether the holes were included.
The First Wave ribbon marked Pavel "Tin" Satan as an early volunteer. At R-F13, a newcomer asked what those first days had been like.
Pavel "Tin" Satan walked the captured trenches of Verdel Ridge and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.
Rain washed the chalk names from the trench signs. Pavel "Tin" Satan spent the evening directing strangers past the same junction.
Pavel "Tin" Satan saved a seat for someone fetching supper. Holding it against three hungry men turned out to be hard work.
After the shelling at R-F13, nobody could account for Pavel "Tin" Satan. His kit remains beside the bunk.
knightowlvt: Emil "Shadow" Knightowlvt stepped off the supply cart at R-F12 and stood very still, listening to the guns as if they were saying his name.
Emil "Shadow" Knightowlvt was among the first hundred through the depot gates. The First Wave ribbon is the only clean thing he owns.
Victory at Verdel Ridge. Emil "Shadow" Knightowlvt let himself talk about leave for the first time in days.
Emil "Shadow" Knightowlvt saved a seat for someone fetching supper. Holding it against three hungry men turned out to be hard work.
The listening post reported scraping beyond the wire. Emil "Shadow" Knightowlvt waited through an hour of it before a loose stake was found.
Emil "Shadow" Knightowlvt spent the night in no man's land with pliers and a roll of wire. Every flare meant lying flat in the mud. The gap at R-F12 is closed now.
robertoneill2008: Dorian Robertoneill came up with a draft of replacements on Day 4. Nobody asked his name until the third night. After that, everyone knew it.
Dorian Robertoneill found water collecting beneath the gun's cover. He sketched a small shelter and took the drawing to the stores.
Dorian Robertoneill was on wiring party in no man's land. Every time a flare went up he froze like a scarecrow. It worked.
